programs, and the W69a fill-audit residue. _Mechanism (the pointer arm):_
`GlobalLetBinding::Disposition` gains `PromoteObject` — the
`ValueRepr::Pointer` case (classes, choices, multi-element tuples/structs)
now promotes instead of Declining. The dispatch is unchanged in structure:
object-identical `Copy` → the W69a store/load `Promote`; `Pointer` →
`PromoteObject`; `None` → `NoStorage` (still dead defensive per the W69a
fill audit); non-object-copy `Copy`/`Custom` and unmapped chase shapes →
`Declined` FATAL (message retexted to name what remains declined). A
`PromoteObject` binding's backing global holds the OBJECT representation
(`GetType(type_id)`, exactly what `GetOrCreateGlobalLetVariable` already
built), `PrepareGlobalLetDefinitions` zero-initializes it identically, and
the ctor hook fills it with a MEMCPY of the object's alloc size from the
bound value's lowered pointer — mirrored precedent:
`FunctionContext::CopyObject` (function_context.cpp), whose body is now
shared through a new public `CopyObject(TypeInFile, llvm::Value*
source_addr, llvm::Value* dest_addr)` overload that the inst-id form
delegates to. The bound value's lowered value IS a pointer because
`AcquireValue`'s `Pointer` arm forwards the acquired ref's address
(handle_expr_category.cpp), and the source is the binding's own
materialized temporary (nothing can alias it — values cannot have their
address taken), so the copy rides the values.md as-if license (§6 R-3).
References: `TryEmitGlobalLetValue`'s `PromoteObject` arm serves the
global's ADDRESS as the value representation — the same shape
`FileContext::GetConstant`'s pointer-value-rep arm serves for constants
and a by-value parameter carries — with `AddGlobalToCurrentFingerprint` on
every hit, same as the `Promote` arm. handle.cpp's NameRef comment
retexted (copy-of-object OR pointer now served; class-scope statics and
namespace-scope bindings still excluded). import_ref.cpp and check
untouched; SemIR untouched. _The ledger acceptance test (OQ-3):_

### W8c records the §1.3 all-expression alternative equality call (2026-09-25)

The design (pattern_matching.md:487-497) says an alternative pattern
whose payload list contains NO proper patterns — `case .Ok(42)` —
"behaves like an expression pattern": whole-value `==` on the
constructed choice value. In-slice choices implement no `Core.EqWith`,
so the literal reading would reject every such pattern. Recorded call
(OQ-3, adopted 2026-08-18, landed at W8a): the all-expression payload
list is implemented IDENTICALLY to the mixed case — the discriminant
test, then elementwise `==` on the payload in a block dominated by
that test (`MatchCaseAlternativePatternMatch`, pattern_match.cpp:561).
This is observationally equivalent to the specified whole-value `==`
for choice types with structural equality, which is the only equality
these choices could have; the equivalence breaks the day user-defined
`EqWith` on choices exists, which is when this entry is re-examined.
Coverage keeps the design's refutability reading
(pattern_matching.md:589-594): a constant-payload arm such as
`.Some(42)` is refutable and records NOTHING toward exhaustiveness
(the `payload_is_irrefutable` classification, pinned by
fail_nonexhaustive_payload_literal.carbon). Veto-able.

### W8c records the §4 R-3 evaluation-order approximation (2026-09-25)

The design interleaves pattern-match evaluation with binding
initialization and destruction (pattern_matching.md:776-791: a
`var y: X` element is initialized, the sibling `0` tested, `y`
destroyed on failure) and orders side-effectful pattern evaluation
(:834-952), with left-to-right short-circuit across tuple elements
(:100-118). The fork's match arms instead run a two-pass split — every
arm condition is emitted in the test pass and bindings initialize
afterward in the bind pass (`EmitCaseArmTestAndBind`,
handle_match.cpp:564) — and tuple-element conditions are emitted
eagerly into one block and folded flat (`FoldMatchCaseConditions`,
pattern_match.cpp:766) rather than short-circuited per element.
Recorded approximation (plan §2.1(a)(i) and §4 R-3): this is
observationally equivalent BECAUSE in-slice scrutinee and element
types are trivially copyable integers and choices of those (total
reads — no observable copies or destructions to mis-order) and
in-slice case expressions are constants (no effects to sequence). The
one ordering kept as MANDATORY structure is discriminant-then-payload
dominance (the explicit block switch in
`MatchCaseAlternativePatternMatch`), which is R-2 poison safety, not
part of the approximation. The design's "Destroyed!" example is
inexpressible in-slice — exactly why the approximation is safe today.
Re-examined the day non-trivial types pass the scrutinee gate
(handle_match.cpp:238). Veto-able.

owns its value, and filed the three defects that kept the 0.1 toolchain from
implementing it. Measured at OP-2's planning, two of the three are toolchain
defects that upstream still carries (upstream trunk d4f1ec203): lowering treated
an `as_compatible` of a value as a no-op whatever the two value representations,
which can differ for `MaybeUnformed(T)` since upstream PR 6334 (fork plan M-2,
M-3), and the toolchain treated every adapter as trivially destructible, so the
default storage's own `Destroy` could never run under the `Core.Optional`
adapter (M-5). Both are fixed at the root. The adapter rule is a fork design
decision, minted here as F-016 (D-OP2-11): "an adapter is destroyed as its
adapted type, and is trivially destructible exactly when that type is". V-3
holds, as the plan's head states it: no accepted proposal or leads' direction is
contradicted; both toolchain fixes repair upstream code that upstream's own head
still carries; F-016 fills a silence of the adapter rules (read literally,
classes.md's `TrivialDestructor` rule makes every adapter without a destructor
trivially destructible, since an adapter declares no data members, and F-016
decides that an adapter's data is its adapted object, generics/details.md:223
and :1910, "the same data representation"); the one consequence that departs
from C++, `Core.Optional(i32)` not being trivially destructible where
`std::optional<int>` is, is filed as W-196 rather than claimed as design;
D-OP2-15 narrows F-015's API (only `Core.Optional(T*)` is `UnformedInit`), which
leaves 0.1 short of proposal p000257's direction that an `Optional(T)` gives any
payload an unformed state, a filed limit (W-200), not a rule against the
proposal; and D-OP2-16 amends D-OP-13's gate phrase "a conformance run of
record" while Actions is disabled, departing from SL-2's practice of keeping a
row PARTIAL until its run of record (plan §7 A-14). F-016, D-OP2-15 and D-OP2-16
are recorded for after-the-fact veto (R29(a)), below. Landed on
claude/carbon-fork-0-1-op2, stacked on PR 56's head 379f20f67 (OP-1, held open),
in the commits fork/optional2/plan.md §3 fixed, after the plan's 963adda99 (rev
1), 4027885b3 (rev 2, plan reviews A and B folded) and a5b81889b (rev 3, the
focused re-review folded, signed off): 757cd0e74 (commit 2: the three toolchain
files, the prelude and the five golden sources without CHECK lines), 189baa262
(commit 3, "Autoupdate testdata goldens on the container arbiter"), 503d25895
(commit 4: the programs, the oracle, the program table, optional.md, the
classes.md F-016 amendment and the row), 9f9ccd768 and f859c7e73 (the fold of
the two implementation reviews), c396efeae (the merge of trunk f67ab650d,
fork/ORCHESTRATION.md only) and the discharge commit carrying this entry. This
entry is the decision record F-016.

F-016, the design text, as landed in docs/design/classes.md:1804-1814 (a dated
blockquote after the adapter rules, before "Inside an adapter, the `Self` type
matches the adapter."; its two links shown as their text): "An adapter declares
no fields and has the same data representation as its adapted type (Generics:
adapting types), so its object is an object of the adapted type, and that object
is the adapter's data member for the `TrivialDestructor` rule under Destructors.
Destroying an adapter destroys that object as the adapted type's destructor
does, and an adapter is trivially destructible exactly when its adapted type is.
So an adapter may implement `UnformedInit`, whose unformed object is left
uninitialized in 0.1, only when its adapted type's destructor accepts such an
object. The fork's 0.1 toolchain implements this (fork/optional2/plan.md,
D-OP2-3); before it, an adapter's object was never destroyed." Rationale
(D-OP2-3, D-OP2-11): classes.md:1789-1799 gives an adapter no fields and makes
it compatible with the adapted type, and generics/details.md:223 and :1910 give
it "the same data representation", so its object is the adapted object;
`IsTriviallyDestructible` already walked an adapter into its adapted type for
the union and C++ export predicates, and only the destroy synthesis disagreed.
Break condition: an accepted upstream design specifies adapter destruction
otherwise, or this entry's veto rejects F-016; the custom_witness.cpp hunks then
follow it (D-OP2-3).

THE DECISIONS, D-OP2-1 to D-OP2-16, verbatim from fork/optional2/plan.md §0.4 as
folded through the two plan reviews (A-1 to A-7; B-1, B-M1 to B-M5 and B-m1 to
B-m7), the focused re-review (RR-1 to RR-5) and the implementation review fold
(R2-M1, R2-m1); each break condition is the decision's own, and the `§`, `M-`,
`R-`, `A-` and row references are the plan's:

-   **D-OP2-1: W-171 is fixed where it is caused, in lowering: an
    `as_compatible` of a value converts between its operand's and its result's
    value representations.** A pointer representation to a copy one loads the
    object as the result type (`LoadObject`); a copy to a pointer stores the
    value into a new `alloca` of the result type and yields its address
    (`CreateAlloca`, `StoreObject`); equal kinds stay a no-op; any other pair
    of differing kinds fails a CHECK that names both representations, since
    `MaybeUnformed` also turns a `Custom` representation into a pointer, which
    no type produces today and which would otherwise be read with the old
    silent no-op (M-21; amended 2026-10-14, review fold: A-5). The invariant,
    in one sentence: compatible types share an object representation but not
    necessarily a value representation (type_completion.cpp:809-832), and in a
    generic only the specific being lowered knows which (R17). It is the root
    cause of the three escapes of M-2 (the concrete CHECK, the generic, the
    adapter-stripped explicit `unsafe as`), because all three are value
    conversions that end in the same no-op (handle.cpp:98-101) applied to two
    different representations, and only lowering sees the specific; the check
    side cannot, since both representations are `Dependent` there. The same
    defect exists for an initializing `as_compatible` whose two init
    representations differ (M-18): its fix needs storage for the in-place
    side, which the checker assigns (§7 A-15), and no operation of
    `Core.Optional` reaches it, so it is filed as W-198, not claimed (amended
    2026-10-14, review fold: A-2). `GetValueRepr` already adds the
    kinds to the specific's fingerprint (lower/function_context.cpp:450-457),
    so specifics that differ only in representation are never coalesced
    (M-12: `Unwrap` lowers to three distinct specifics for `bool`, `i32` and
    `Core.Optional(i32*)`). Break condition: upstream fixes the defect another
    way (for example a dedicated SemIR conversion); the next upstream advance
    takes upstream's fix and drops this hunk if upstream's makes the three
    probes of M-2 and the two W-171 arbiters pass.
-   **D-OP2-2: convert.cpp's check-side round trip stays, with its CHECK testing
    the operand.** The two `ValueRepr::ForType` calls swap their type
    arguments (two lines), so `unformed_value_rep` is the `MaybeUnformed(T)`
    operand's, as the comment above them says ("`MaybeUnformed(T)` might have a
    pointer value representation when `T` does not"), and the unchanged
    `CARBON_CHECK(unformed_value_rep.kind == SemIR::ValueRepr::Pointer)` then
    states a true invariant: the two kinds differ only when the operand's is a
    pointer (type_completion.cpp:816-827 can only turn `T`'s representation into
    a pointer). The concrete `MaybeUnformed(bool) unsafe as bool` then emits
    `value_as_ref`, `as_compatible` on a reference and `acquire_value` (§4),
    which lowering's new conversion never sees (it acts on values only).
    Deleting the round trip instead (variant **b**, M-4) changes the same zero
    goldens, but deletes upstream code; the two-line correction is the
    smaller divergence (V-3). Break condition: upstream rewrites or deletes the
    block; this hunk follows it.
-   **D-OP2-3: an adapter is destroyed as its adapted type.** In
    custom_witness.cpp, `CanDestroyClass` returns `NonTrivial` for an adapter
    whose adapted type has destruction work and `Trivial` otherwise, and
    `MakeSubobjectDestroyOpBody`'s class arm, for such an adapter, converts
    `self` to the adapted type (`as_compatible` on the reference) and calls its
    `SelfDestruct`; "destruction work" is the existing union and export
    predicate, `!IsTriviallyDestructible(adapted)`, guarded against an
    error-typed adapted type (M-7's variant **c**). One sentence (R17): an
    adapter declares no fields and has "the same data representation" as its
    adapted type (classes.md:1789-1799; generics/details.md:223, :1910), so its
    object is the adapted object and its destruction is that type's, which is
    fork design F-016 (D-OP2-11), the reading under which the
    `TrivialDestructor` rule's "data members" of an adapter are its adapted
    object (amended 2026-10-14, review fold: A-6, B-M2). It is the root
    cause of W-170 because the storage's own `Destroy` is unreachable without
    it (M-5); it is also a general defect (M-5's adapter_destroy), fixed for
    every adapter, upstream's included (M-5). `IsTriviallyDestructible`
    already walks an adapter into its adapted type (:886-893), so the union and
    C++ export predicates already agreed with this rule; only the destroy
    synthesis disagreed. Break condition: an accepted upstream design or
    upstream change specifies adapter destruction otherwise; this hunk follows
    it, and the Optional storage's destroy moves to wherever that design puts
    it.
-   **D-OP2-4: the default storage declares the destroy; `Optional` and the
    pointer niche do not.** `impl forall [T: Copy & Destroy]
    DefaultOptionalStorage(T) as Destroy` whose `Op` destroys
    `self.value unsafe as T` when `self.has_value` is true: p001154's sketch
    (`if (me.holds_value) value.Destroy();`), on the storage rather than on
    `Optional`, because an impl keyed on `Optional` reaches `Optional(T*)` and
    breaks union fields (M-6), while one keyed on `DefaultOptionalStorage`
    cannot reach the niche, which adapts `MaybeUnformed(T*)` (M-7: unions of
    `Core.Optional(i32*)` and `Core.Optional(C*)` still compile). The fields
    themselves need nothing more: `MaybeUnformed(T)` never destroys (§0.1 row
    5) and `bool` is trivial, and a class's declared `Destroy` does not destroy
    its fields anyway (W-126; rev 1's W-197, amended 2026-10-14, review fold:
    B-M5), so nothing is destroyed twice. Copy semantics
    are unchanged: `Optional(T) as Copy` (:50-54) still copies the value once
    through the storage's `Copy`, and the copy and the original each destroy
    their own (M-9). Break condition: a `Core.Optional(T*)` union field or the
    C++ pointer mapping of `Core.Optional(T*)` regresses in the gate or the
    conformance suite (none measured, M-7, M-13, M-22), or W-196's conditional
    triviality lands; the impl then moves or gains that condition. A
    `Core.Optional(i32)` union field, rejected and pinned by the
    `fail_union_value_field` split, is D-OP2-6's accepted consequence and does
    not trigger it (amended 2026-10-14, review fold: B-M1).
-   **D-OP2-5: `OptionalStorage.Type` is `Destroy` (`let Type: Destroy;` in
    place of `let Type: type;`).** Without it a checked generic cannot destroy
    an `Optional(T)` it creates (M-8), which is W-170's own measured
    consequence (its notes, and optional.md:284-290); with it the storage type
    is known destroyable under the generic's bound, and both storage impls
    satisfy it (`DefaultOptionalStorage(T)` by D-OP2-4, `MaybeUnformed(T*)`
    trivially). It costs 13 refills (M-8): SemIR in nine check goldens, and,
    in four lower goldens (builtins/cpp, union/basic,
    interop/cpp/std_initializer_list_pointer_pointer and
    std_initializer_list_pointer_size), reordered definitions and unreferenced
    no-op `weak_odr` `SelfDestruct` definitions of pointer-niche specifics,
    whose `MaybeUnformed(T*)` storage (optional.carbon:189) now needs a
    `Destroy` witness (rev 3 said "13 SemIR-only refills"; amended 2026-10-14,
    implementation review fold: R2-m1). Break condition: the storage leaves
    the public API (W-176) or upstream's `Optional` design changes the storage
    interface; the bound moves with it.
-   **D-OP2-6: `Core.Optional(T)` for a non-pointer `T` is not trivially
    destructible, even when `T` is, and W-170's break condition is amended to
    match.** Its storage defines a destructor with a non-empty body, which
    classes.md:1992-2003 makes not `TrivialDestructor`, and by F-016 the
    `Optional` adapter is trivially destructible exactly when its storage is
    (rev 1 attributed this to classes.md alone; amended 2026-10-14, review
    fold: B-M2); the conditional triviality of C++'s `std::optional`
    ([optional.dtor]: "If `is_trivially_destructible_v<T>` is true, then this
    destructor is trivial") is p001154's considered, not adopted, alternative.
    Measured consequences: a union field of type `Core.Optional(i32)`, which
    OP-1 admitted only because nothing was destroyed, is now
    `UnionFieldNotTriviallyCopyable` (M-7), as unions.md:226-228's predicate
    ("no destructor anywhere in the type or its subobjects") says, and
    unions.md admits `Core.Optional(T*)` fields and names no other Optional
    (:233-238); a `for` loop over `Core.Range` runs, per iteration, a second
    out-of-line call of the no-op `i32` `SelfDestruct` and a store, a reload
    and a branch on `has_value`, eight more optimized instructions in the
    function (M-10, M-20; amended 2026-10-14, review fold: A-4). C++ export is
    not affected: a Carbon class with a `Core.Optional(i32)` field does not
    map to C++ as a complete type before or after OP-2 (W-049, M-22), and rev
    1's sentence that it exports with a destructor was unmeasured and false
    (amended 2026-10-14, review fold: B-M1, A-7). Filed as W-196 (§1.7), not
    row-bounding: no operation of `Core.Optional` fails. This amends W-170's
    break condition, which OP-1 wrote as "a `Destroy` for `Core.Optional` that
    keeps `Core.Optional(T*)` trivially destructible lands with no union or
    interop regression, and optional_destroys_value un-SKIPs to PASS in a
    conformance run of record", to "a `Destroy` for `Core.Optional` that keeps
    `Core.Optional(T*)` trivially destructible lands with no regression of a
    `Core.Optional(T*)` union field or of the C++ pointer mapping, and
    optional_destroys_value un-SKIPs to PASS in a conformance run of record
    (D-OP2-16)": the one union regression is for a non-pointer payload, which
    unions.md never named, and follows from unions.md's own predicate, so it is
    filed as W-196, and W-170's discharge notes quote both texts (amended
    2026-10-14, review fold: B-M1). Break condition: an accepted design adopts
    conditional `TrivialDestructor` (or an equivalent), or a program needs an
    `Optional` of a non-pointer in a union or in a loop whose cost is measured
    beyond the safety strategy's budget; W-196 then lands that rule, or §7
    A-11's scalar storage as an interim fix.
-   **D-OP2-7: W-173 is a fail-stop in `Get()`, not a TY4 amendment.** `Get()`
    on an empty value writes `carbon: Core.Optional.Get on an empty value;
    terminating` to stderr and aborts, through the `"fail_stop"` builtin, as a
    `Core.Slice` bounds violation does (D-SL-4), so `Get()` never reads unformed
    storage and never returns the niche's null pointer, and TY4 holds as
    written ("the only way to reach the pointee of an `Optional(T*)` is through
    `Get` after `HasValue`"; a `Get` without `HasValue` now stops before any
    pointer exists). It is the close condition F-015 already wrote for W-173
    (optional.md:481-482) and SAFE-1's D-SAFE-14 (fail-stop, never a flag).
    Cost, measured: nothing in the optimized `for` loop, whose `HasValue()`
    test makes the check dead (M-10); a test and a branch in each unoptimized
    `Get` specific; 15 goldens on its own, all within the 28 (M-10). TY4's
    amendment path is the rejected alternative (§7 A-7): it would weaken a
    safety rule to describe a defect. Break condition: a measured program or
    benchmark where the check is not folded and costs more than the strategy's
    budget; then a per-site unchecked accessor with an `unsafe` marker is
    added beside `Get()` (D-SAFE-14's form), and `Get()` stays checked.
-   **D-OP2-8: no existing line of optional.carbon moves (D-OP-8 carried).**
    Four places change in place (:48 added at rev 2 by D-OP2-15; amended
    2026-10-14, review fold: A-1): :48, the `UnformedInit` impl, becomes a

    library "prelude/types/string";` (the `str` that `"fail_stop"` takes is

    Why it matters beyond goldens: SAFE-1's pages (PR 53) cite optional.carbon

-   **D-OP2-9: conformance.** The three arbiters un-SKIP with their EXPECT

-   **D-OP2-10: goldens: five new CHECK-free sources, 28 refills, no hand

    check/testdata/as/maybe_unformed_value_repr.carbon,

-   **D-OP2-11: docs: F-015's page is updated in place with a dated status
    line; the adapter rule is minted as fork design F-016 and recorded on
    classes.md as a dated amendment (amended 2026-10-14, review fold: B-M2,
    A-6).** docs/design/optional.md is the fork's own page: its status line
    names OP-2 and its date, the paragraphs about W-170, W-171 and W-173 are
    replaced by the landed rules, the `UnformedInit` row narrows (D-OP2-15),
    and its 0.1 limits lose three items and gain W-196, W-199, W-200 and PR
    51's W-126 (§2.5). classes.md, upstream's page, gets a dated blockquote
    after its adapter rules (amendments, never rewrites), labelled with F-016,
    as every fork amendment of an upstream page names its F-id
    (docs/design/control_flow/loops.md:116, docs/design/README.md:862). F-016
    reads: "an adapter is destroyed as its adapted type, and is trivially
    destructible exactly when that type is". Rev 1 held that classes.md
    implied it and minted nothing, with the break condition "a reviewer shows
    that D-OP2-3 or D-OP2-6 decides something no design page implies; it is
    then minted as F-016". Review B showed it: read literally, the
    `TrivialDestructor` rule (classes.md:1995-1999) makes an adapter without a
    destructor trivially destructible, since it declares no data members, and
    only the reading that the adapted object is the adapter's data

THE DECISIONS, D-OP-1 to D-OP-15, verbatim from fork/optional/plan.md §0.4 as
folded through the two plan reviews (A-1 to A-10, B-1 to B-9) and the
implementation review fold (R1-1 to R1-7, IR2-1 to IR2-12), except that the
residue the plan calls W-190 reads W-195, its id as re-allocated at this
discharge; each break condition is the decision's own, and the `§`, `M-`, `R-`
and row references are the plan's:

-   **D-OP-1: equality.** Two empty Optionals are equal; an empty and a
    non-empty Optional are unequal; two non-empty Optionals are equal exactly
    when their values are equal under `T`'s `==`, and `!=` is `T`'s `!=` on two
    non-empty operands (C++ [optional.relops] uses the contained type's
    corresponding operator; every prelude same-type impl defines `NotEqual`
    explicitly, int.carbon:93-96, char.carbon:49-52). An accepted design already
    presupposes this `==`: "a pattern of the form `Optional(T).None` is an
    expression pattern and is compared using `==`" (p002188:488-489,
    pattern_matching.md:527-528), which spells the empty value as a value where
    F-015 keeps the function `None()` (V-3) (amended 2026-10-13, review fold:
    A-9). This is Rust's derived `PartialEq` for `Option` and C++'s
    `operator==`/`operator!=` for `std::optional`; the two agree, so a C++17
    differential oracle is legitimate (R30 does not apply: the two sides agree
    by construction). It is an equivalence when `T`'s is, and refines the order
    of D-OP-2 when `T`'s `==` refines `T`'s order
    (comparison_operators.md:466-472). Break condition: an accepted upstream
    design for `Core.Optional` specifies a different equality; the impl bodies
    and the oracle follow it.
-   **D-OP-2: ordering, with only `Ordered` required.** An empty Optional orders
    before every non-empty one, two empty ones are equivalent, and two non-empty
    ones order as their values under `T`'s four operators; `Less`,
    `LessOrEquivalent`, `Greater` and `GreaterOrEquivalent` are C++'s `<`, `<=`,
    `>` and `>=` for `std::optional` term for term ([optional.relops]) and
    Rust's derived `PartialOrd` ("`None` compares less than any `Some`"). The
    impl needs `T: Ordered` only, not `Eq`, because
    comparison_operators.md:468-469 imposes no such requirement and C++ does not
    (measured: an ordered-only payload's Optionals order and do not compare
    equal, M-10). Transitivity and consistency under reversal (:436-465) carry
    over from `T`'s. Break condition: upstream decides that `Optional` is not
    ordered or orders `None` last; the `OrderedWith` impl is deleted or its four
    bodies changed, and `optional_compare_diff` with them.
-   **D-OP-3: the spelling
    `final impl forall [T: Destroy & OptionalStorage & Eq] Optional(T) as EqWith(Optional(T))`
    and its `Ordered` twin.** The constraints `Eq`/`Ordered`
    (comparison.carbon:19-21, :34-36) because `[T: EqWith(T)]` is "name `T` not
    found" (M-2); `OptionalStorage` because the class forces it (:30); `Destroy`
    because each `Get()` copy is destroyed (M-2, the `Try` impl's bound for the
    same reason, :62-64); the conditional form is details.md's conditional
    conformance (:4457-4469), whose own example is comparing containers of
    comparable elements. `final`: EqWith and OrderedWith have no associated
    constants, so `final` is not needed for generic code to type-check (both
    variants check, M-3); it is chosen because comparison is part of the type's
    definition, so when the payload is `Core.Eq` (and `Destroy`) a payload
    type's library cannot change what `==` means on its Optionals (M-11: without
    `final` a user impl silently wins), while for a payload that is not
    `Core.Eq` the final impl does not match and that library's `impl Optional(Q)
    as EqWith(Optional(Q))` is legal and defines `==` (amended 2026-10-13,
    review fold: A-10); the prelude's integer comparison impls (cross-width,
    `Int(N)` with `Int(M)`) and its float and C++-integer ones are `final` too
    (int.carbon:93-104, float.carbon:165-170, cpp/int.carbon:341-375; corrected
    2026-10-13, implementation review fold: IR2-5) and so is the `Try` impl
    (:69; for `Try`, `final` is load-bearing, because generic code reads its
    associated constants `ContinueType` and `BreakType`, details.md:5262-5379,
    and R27 records the W-072 incident that restored the sketch's `final`). The
    `final` impls may be declared here: optional.carbon declares the root of the
    `Self` type (details.md:5381-5395). p5337:280-286 makes a non-final impl
    that a final impl completely subsumes an error; the 0.1 toolchain diagnoses
    it only where it is used (M-11: the declaration alone compiles), which the
    `fail_specialize` and `todo_fail_specialize_unused` splits pin (§2.3) and
    W-179 files (amended 2026-10-13, review fold: A-10). Break condition: a
    payload type needs its own Optional equality (for example a niche-aware
    one); `final` is dropped, which changes only the `fail_specialize` and
    `todo_fail_specialize_unused` splits of §2.3.
-   **D-OP-4: bodies over `HasValue()` and `Get()`, no builtin, no
    storage-interface change.** Each function tests `HasValue()` before calling
    `Get()`, so an empty operand's unformed storage is never read (W-173 is
    about `Get()` on an empty value, which the impls never do); `Get()` returns
    a copy, destroyed by the end of the call, and the operands are neither moved
    nor destroyed (M-5). Comparing in place through a storage-level `Equal`
    would need a new member of the private `OptionalStorage` (:16-26)
    implemented for the pointer niche too, where it needs pointer equality
    (W-174), for no 0.1 benefit; the copy is the placeholder API's documented
    cost (:23-24). That cost is observable: for a `T` whose `Copy` or `Destroy`
    has an effect, each comparison of two non-empty operands runs each once per
    value (M-5), a divergence from comparison_operators.md:316 and :434 ("should
    have no observable side-effects") that V-3 discloses and F-015 states
    (amended 2026-10-13, review fold: A-2). Break condition: `Optional` becomes
    matchable (W-177) or a by-reference accessor lands; the bodies then compare
    in place, with no `Copy` or `Destroy` of `T`, the signatures unchanged, and
    the divergence entry of the V-3a register is closed (amended 2026-10-13,
    review fold: A-2).
-   **D-OP-5: same-type comparisons only.** `Optional(T)` compares with
    `Optional(T)`: not with a `T` (`o == 5`, measured rejected), not with
    `Cpp.nullptr`, and not with `Optional(U)` for `U != T` (measured rejected).
    comparison_operators.md:288-289 selects `EqWith` "without considering
    possible implicit conversions" and names the `like` operator as the way to
    admit them (:289-300), which the toolchain does not parse (M-10, W-178);
    details.md:4466-4469's conditional-conformance example compares containers
    "with the same element type"; Rust's `Option<T>: PartialEq<Option<T>>`
    agrees. C++'s mixed operators (`opt == value`, `opt == std::nullopt`,
    `optional<T> == optional<U>`) are rejected alternatives (§7 A-1, A-2). Break
    condition: `like` lands (W-178); the impls become `impl like Optional(T) as
    EqWith(like Optional(T))` if the design then says so.

RESIDUE, filed at this discharge, each `{id, kind, title, subsystem, size,
bullet, evidence, blocked_by, notes}` with its mechanism and break condition, as
fork/optional/plan.md §2.6 tables them. The ids are the block W-170 to W-179
that trunk 162c7e839's fork/ORCHESTRATION.md reserves for OP-1 ("ids from W-170
and fork design id F-015 if minted"), all ten used, and W-195. The re-scan
immediately before this commit read the maximum filed id of
fork/inventory/work-items.json on 71 refs (trunk, origin/trunk and the 69 local
and origin `claude/carbon-fork-0-1-*` refs): trunk W-125 (and the op and dd
branches, which carry trunk's ledger), ua2 W-127, cmake W-133, safe W-150, ev
W-155, st W-167, sc W-168 (head df5120d03); no ref files any of W-169 and above,
and no text on any ref names W-170 to W-179 except trunk's reservation and
DD-1's plan, which records them as OP-1's. W-190, which the plan and the
implementation review fold gave the R1-4 residue as "the first id after DD-1's
W-180..W-189", is taken: DD-1's plan rev 2 (claude/carbon-fork-0-1-dd at
a1d96520a, fork/designdocs/plan.md, committed before the fold) reserves
W-180..W-194 and gives W-190 to a different defect. By the plan's rule (§2.6)
the residue takes the maximum plus one, skipping every reserved block (W-169
SC-1's, W-170 to W-179 OP-1's, W-180 to W-194 DD-1's): W-195, renumbered in
docs/design/optional.md in this commit. W-170 (missing-feature, Optional bullet,
row-bounding): a `Core.Optional` never destroys the value it holds; the default
storage's `MaybeUnformed(T)` runs no destructor (optional.carbon:140-143), and
M-6's `Destroy` prototype fixes it but makes `Core.Optional(i32*)` union fields
`UnionFieldNotTriviallyCopyable` and moves 26 goldens; arbiter
optional_destroys_value. W-171 (toolchain-defect, Optional bullet,
row-bounding): the default storage mis-lowers `MaybeUnformed(T) unsafe as T`
when `T`'s value representation differs, so `Get()` and copy crash the compiler
for `bool` and silently return the storage address for a nested
`Core.Optional(U*)`; arbiters optional_bool and optional_nested_pointer. W-172
(toolchain-defect, generics bullet): a float or character literal argument for a
`T: Core.Copy & Core.Destroy` parameter aborts check in `CanDestroyType`. W-173
(missing-feature, Optional bullet): `Get()` on an empty value is unchecked.
W-174 (design-needed, pointer types bullet): the built-in pointer types have no
`==`, so `Core.Optional(T*)` compares only when `T*` is `Core.Eq`; arbiter
optional_pointer_compare, which does not bound the row. W-175 (missing-feature,
Optional bullet): no explicit `as` between Optionals. W-176 (missing-feature,
Optional bullet): `T` must be `Core.Copy & Core.Destroy` or a pointer, through
the private `OptionalStorage`. W-177 (missing-feature, the sum-type consumption
bullet): `Core.Optional` is not matchable; related to W-011, and SAFE-1's EX-M-5
and EX-M-6 wait on it. W-178 (missing-feature, checked generics bullet): the
`like` operator is not parsed. W-179 (toolchain-defect, checked generics bullet,
review A's A-10): a non-final impl that a `final` impl completely subsumes is
diagnosed only where it is used. W-195 (toolchain-defect, generics bullet,
implementation review R1-4): a checked generic body that applies a
compile-time-only operation to a symbolic `T` (`Core.IntLiteral`'s `==`) aborts
lowering instead of being evaluated or diagnosed. W-172, W-174, W-178, W-179 and
W-195 are ledger items only: rows 51, 52 and 75 keep their text, which none of
them falsifies. Row 68 gains the clause "`Core.Optional` itself is not matchable
(W-177, F-015)". Named, not re-filed: assignment does not destroy the

> **F-015 amendment (2026-11-05, SV-1, F-020; re-derived by FO-1 after DR-1's
> W-322).** The `std::optional` mapping this design deferred to W-011
> relates to `Core.Optional(T)`: a C++ `std::optional<T>` converts to and
> from `Core.Optional(T)` in one implicit step for a non-pointer `T` that
> is a concrete scalar or pointer payload type (through
> `Core.CppCompat.StdOptional(T)` and two prelude `ImplicitAs` impls that
> use only the public API), and a `Core.Optional(T)` argument is offered to
> C++ overload resolution as `std::optional<T>`. A `Core.Optional(T)` is
> not matched through that choice (D-SV-7's view, retired by DR-1,
> W-322). The class, its API, its storage, the `Try` impl and
> `Core.Optional(T*)`'s pointer mapping are unchanged;
> docs/design/optional.md's "C++ interoperability" paragraph says so.
> W-177 stays open. Veto-able with F-020.

WHAT LANDED, by commit. C1 (A1 to A7, B1 to B5; convert.cpp, pending_block.h,
handle_loop_statement.cpp, sem_ir/expr_info.{h,cpp}, lower/aggregate.cpp,
lower/file_context.cpp, lower/function_context.cpp, lower/handle.cpp,
lower/handle_expr_category.cpp): a template-dependent operand initialized into
storage of its own type is a storage-carrying `InitializeAction` whose storage
is a copy of its access chain (`CloneStorageAccessChain`) that each specific
places; replayed initializing conversions get a local storage access block;
`FindStorageArgForInitializer` reads the specific; a dependent value conversion
is a `ConvertToValueAction`; a template-dependent array, union or class value is
converted whole for each instantiation, a class value only when its source names
exactly its fields; the `for` cursor pointer type is required complete; lowering
reads categories, constants and storage in the specific, and an inexact function
type with a return slot is a CHECK. C2 (import_ref.cpp, stringify.cpp): a
generic whose definition is resolved per instantiation, used from another
library, is one `semantics TODO` at the `import`, and a diagnostic prints a
dependent operation as its expression. C3 (inst_kind.def, typed_insts.h,
diagnostic_helpers.h, pointer_dereference.{h,cpp}, handle_operator.cpp,
handle_name.cpp, member_access.{h,cpp}, handle_index.cpp, call.cpp):
`PointerDereferenceAction`, `AddrOfAction`, `TupleIndexAction` and
`IndexAction`, created only for an opaque template-dependent operand, and the
callee rule of p2875 for a function-typed value with no constant value. C4
(call.cpp, impl_lookup.cpp): `IsCallPerformable` forms a generic class type with
template-dependent argument values in the definition, so deduction sees through
`Holder(T)`, and impl lookup for a query that names a template binding selects
no impl in the definition (`QueryNamesTemplateBinding`), so `var y: T;` resolves
`DefaultOrUnformed` on instantiation. C5 (member_access.cpp,
diagnostics/kind.def): on instantiation a member of a template-dependent operand
is looked up in the argument type and in the parameter's constraint, and
different entities are `TemplateMemberLookupAmbiguous`. P: eight programs under
the bullet, one with a C++ oracle, and the regenerated README table. Fix 1
(lower/function_context.cpp): a constant splice lowers the instructions of its
block that are not constant (D-TP-25), with the ninth program,
templates_constant_elements. Fix 2 (eval.cpp, import_ref.cpp, stringify.cpp,
pointer_dereference.{h,cpp}, a member_access.cpp comment): a runtime array bound
in a specific is an error (D-TP-26), an imported template whose declaration
holds an action reports W-250's TODO (`IsDeclResolvedPerInstantiation`), the six
action kinds a template creates print as expressions, and `const T` and `T.Elem`
are opaque. In all, at the discharge, 26 toolchain source files, 13 new goldens
and 8 refilled (`git diff --stat b2576f6c3 824f29c4e -- toolchain core`: 47
files, +8693/-536), nine programs and one `.diff.cpp` oracle; no core file
changes. The focused re-review of the fold (amended 2026-10-15) adds four fix
commits with their fills and a formatting commit: 632f92117 (eval.cpp,
convert.cpp) diagnoses a runtime operand of any type or always-constant
instruction in a specific (D-TP-26) and converts a spliced tuple element in
each specific (D-TP-6); d8f6ab60a (import_ref.cpp) tests an imported class's,
interface's or named constraint's declaration, definition and member
declarations before loading it (`IsTypeResolvedPerInstantiation`, D-TP-14);
73b3124dd (stringify.cpp) prints a prefix operand of a postfix operation in
parentheses and an interface member as `Interface.Member` (D-TP-23);
67a9dd91c rewraps two calls; and ba64734e7 (eval.cpp, sem_ir/expr_info.cpp,
sem_ir/function.cpp) makes a diagnosed operand an error in the specific's value
block and diagnoses an operand used as a type (D-TP-26). In all, at
1f0bc7be0, 27 toolchain source files, 13 new goldens and 8 refilled (`git diff
--stat b2576f6c3 1f0bc7be0 -- toolchain core`: 48 files, +9674/-537).

THE DECISIONS, D-TP-1 to D-TP-26, verbatim from fork/templates/plan.md §1.14 as
folded through the two plan reviews, the focused re-review and the
implementation review fold; each break condition is the decision's own or the
section's it cites, and the `§`, `RC-`, `TR-` and `W-` references are the
plan's. D-TP-25 and D-TP-26 were added by the implementation review fold;
D-TP-6, D-TP-14, D-TP-18, D-TP-22, D-TP-23 and D-TP-26 were amended by the
focused re-review of the fold (2026-10-15) and are given here as amended.

**D-TP-1.** The slice is crash and miscompile fixes first (R17), then the
rejected dependent forms, then W-183, W-193 and W-127, each IN because its root
cause was found and its cost measured. A template crash whose removal exposes a
miscompile that the same code without a template already has (RC-10's q07c) is
accepted only with the miscompile recorded (W-256), named in the row and on the
page, and kept out of goldens and programs, because the only diagnosis measured
also rejects working programs (§0.3 RC-10, §7.2(11); amended 2026-10-14, review
fold: RR-M2). _Break:_ a review shows a measured cost understated by more than
one fix commit.

**D-TP-2.** Same-type template-dependent initialization is a storage-carrying
`InitializeAction` (§1.2).

**D-TP-3.** The action carries a copy of its storage access chain, and each
specific places it; the body keeps the originals; pending roots are inserted at
the action (§1.2; rewritten 2026-10-14, review fold: A-B1).

**D-TP-4.** Replayed initializing conversions get a local storage access block
(§1.2).

**D-TP-5.** `FindStorageArgForInitializer` is specific-aware; an unresolved
splice has no storage argument (§1.2).

**D-TP-6.** A dependent value conversion is a `ConvertToValueAction`; a
tuple-to-type conversion converts the generic's instruction for a spliced
element's constant (§1.2; (amended 2026-10-15, focused re-review of the fold:
RR1-M2)).

**D-TP-7.** Lowering reads categories, constants and storage in the specific; a
spliced in-place initializer has no value (§1.2).

**D-TP-8.** The `for` cursor pointer type is required complete; an inexact
function type with a return slot is a CHECK (§1.2).

**D-TP-9.** Four action kinds for `*`/`->`, `&`, tuple element access and
indexing, created only for an opaque template-dependent type, qualified or not,
a produced type such as `T.Elem` included (§1.3; amended 2026-10-14, review
fold: A-m7; (amended 2026-10-14, implementation-review fold: IR1-m3)).

**D-TP-10.** A function-typed callee with no constant value calls its type's
function (§1.3).

**D-TP-11.** Generic type constructors with template-dependent argument values
are formed eagerly (§1.6). Round 10 (amended 2026-10-20, round 10: X-1): a type
so formed reaches the refutable-pattern scrutinee gate, which admits a
template-dependent choice or `Core.Int(N)` as it admits a checked generic's, and
an alternative pattern's name is resolved in the choice's own scope in the
definition (`PerformAlternativeAccess`, refutable_binding.cpp:291-304; the
plan's TR-13 amended). _Break:_ a check that reads the shape of a type formed
here and hands a value of it to code that assumes an operation on it was
performed in the definition.

**D-TP-12.** Impl lookup for a query that names a template binding selects no
impl in the definition (§1.7; rewritten 2026-10-14, review fold: A-M4 / B-M5).

**D-TP-13.** Member lookup into a constrained template parameter consults the
type and the constraint on instantiation; different entities, a field beside a
function included, are an error; over SC-1 a template constraint's requirement
defers to the type (§1.5; amended 2026-10-14, review fold: A-M1 / A-M2 / B-M6).

**D-TP-14.** A generic resolved per instantiation, used from another library, is
a `semantics TODO` at the `import`, once, with no cascade, a function or class
template whose declaration holds an action included (§1.2; rewritten 2026-10-14,
review fold: A-m4 / B-m6; (amended 2026-10-14, implementation-review fold:
IR1-M2)), and a class template's field types and member function declarations
and an interface's or named constraint's declaration too; a checked generic
calling an imported `eval fn` is not detected ((amended 2026-10-15, focused
re-review of the fold: RR1-M1 / RR2-M1 / RR1-m2)).

**D-TP-15.** Dropped (A-M3): form parameters are unchanged and filed (W-255).

**D-TP-16.** No upstream cherry-pick; 4a8993af2's representation is used for a
copy, not the shared block (§0.7; amended 2026-10-14, review fold: A-B1).
_Break:_ upstream lands a template commit that subsumes one of C1 to C5 before
TP-1's merge, in which case the plan's next revision takes it as C0 with
upstream authorship.

**D-TP-17.** No fork design id (F-019 unminted): every rule is proposal 2200's,
p2875's or p3763's, and the SC-1 composition rule is SC-1's own D-SC-4. _Break:_
a review shows a rule decided here that proposal 2200 leaves open.

**D-TP-18.** The row stays PARTIAL and W-014 stays OPEN: the first arbiter
clause is met for the four `fail_todo` splits present when W-014 was filed
(TP-1's own `fail_todo` splits, thirty-five since round 5 of the focused

(amended 2026-10-14, review fold: RR-M1 / RR-M2).

**D-TP-19.** Merge after PR 59 with a merge of trunk M, before the
implementation reviews; the PR 58 integration is a separate commit L after them
(§1.12, §3; amended 2026-10-14, review fold: B-B2). In the held state M merges

**D-TP-20.** Nine conformance programs, ten from round 10 (amended 2026-10-20,

**D-TP-21.** DD-1's fixtures flip at land time with unique quotes; resolved
limits get dated notes, never silent deletions; the texts are written in full
and checked by PR 58's checker before L, and L has a document review (§2.9,
Appendix C; amended 2026-10-14, review fold: B-B1). _Break:_ PR 58's checker, as

**D-TP-22.** Commits C1 to C5 with fills, P, M (conflicts only), S (the SC-1
composition rule) and F6, the implementation reviews, at most three fix commits,
L with its document review, R, D last; shrink C5 first, then C3's
`TupleIndexAction` and `IndexAction`; never C1 or C2 (§3; amended 2026-10-14,
review fold: B-B2 / RR-m2). In the held state S, F6 and L are land-time commits,
and the fold used two of the three fix commits for the toolchain and the third
for these records (§1.12, §3; (amended 2026-10-14, implementation-review fold:
IR2-MINOR-10)). The focused re-review of the fold adds four toolchain fix

budget, for the root-cause reason §3's dated note gives; nothing is shrunk
((amended 2026-10-15, focused re-review of the fold: RR1-B1 / RR1-M1 / RR1-M2 /
RR1-m1 / RR2-m6)). Its rounds 2 to 5 add further fix commits with their fills,
and records commits, beyond the budget, each for the reason a dated note in §3

**D-TP-23.** A diagnostic prints a template-dependent operation's splice as its
expression, for every action kind a template creates, with a prefix operand of a
postfix operation in parentheses and an interface member as `Interface.Member`
(§1.2; added 2026-10-14, review fold: A-m2; (amended 2026-10-14,
implementation-review fold: IR1-m2); (amended 2026-10-15, focused re-review of
the fold: RR1-m1 / RR2-m6)).

**D-TP-24.** A template-dependent conversion that would allocate its own
temporary for an array, union or class value is deferred whole; a class value
only when its source names exactly the class's fields (§1.2; added 2026-10-14,
review fold: RR-M1); an initializer of a class whose fields hold an array with a
template-dependent bound or a produced type, such as `T.Item` or `C(M + 1)`, is
deferred whole too, and a class value or initializer of such a class whose
literal omits only fields with a default initializer is deferred as one that
names them all ((amended 2026-10-15, focused re-review of the fold: RR2-1-M2 /
RR4-1-B1)); of any other class, such a literal is converted where the function
is defined and takes the defaults there ((amended 2026-10-15, focused re-review
of the fold: RR5-1-M1 / RR5-1-m1 / RR5r2-M1)), unless an omitted field's
default initializer splices in a template action of the class's generic, such
as `var k: i32 = N + 1;` in `class D(template N: i32)`, when it is deferred too
((amended 2026-10-15, focused re-review of the fold: RR6-1-M1)); a constant
literal nested in a class value, array value or argument that is deferred whole
loses its defaults on instantiation and is rejected with "missing field"
(W-272; (amended 2026-10-15, focused re-review of the fold: RR6r2-M1)).
_Break:_ above.

**D-TP-25.** A constant splice lowers the instructions of its block that are not
constant, where the splice is (§1.2; added 2026-10-14, implementation-review
fold: IR1-B1). _Break:_ above.

**D-TP-26.** In a specific, an operand that is not constant where a type, an
always-constant instruction or an operand used as a type needs a constant is an
error at that operand, and its value in the specific is the error constant
(§1.2; added 2026-10-14, implementation-review fold: IR1-M1; (amended
2026-10-15, focused re-review of the fold: RR1-B1 / RR1-m2)). _Break:_ above.

OPTIONS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED (plan §7.2, each with its evidence there). (1)
Turning every crash into a `semantics TODO`: a Goodhart alternative (R16, R17)
that greens the gate while the forms proposal 2200 makes valid still fail; only
the cross-library form gets a TODO (D-TP-14). (2) Cherry-picking upstream
947c1eb52 to make X31 run: a 131-file language change that leaves X29 and X30
crashing. (3) Cherry-picking upstream 4a8993af2 as C0: measured, its shared
storage access block takes instructions the template body still uses, so nested
literals fail the verifier; its representation is kept for D-TP-3's copy. (4)
Inserting the storage access block where the action is created (rev 1's A4):
measured, b09, b09b, c1, c3 and c4 crash. (5) Deferring every form through
`HandleAction`: changes the SemIR of templates that work today and moves
definition-time errors to instantiation (TR-2). (6) W-183 at the definition
only: proposal 2200 looks in both the type and the constraint and requires
agreement; the definition half is filed (W-260, W-261). (7) W-127 by accepting
the deferred witness only (v6): a final impl is selected in the definition with
an unproven requirement. (8) W-127 by deferring every template-dependent query
(rev 1's v7): two checked-generic goldens changed, one to a misleading
diagnostic. (9) Making action constants structurally canonical for W-254:
touches merge.cpp's comparison, which SC-1 rewrites. (10) Diagnosing template
form parameters (rev 1's D-TP-15): the crash is the same for `generic` (RC-9).
(11) Diagnosing RC-10's shape instead of compiling q07c wrongly: variant g also
rejects k01 and k07, which run, and does not fix the same miscompile without
templates. (12) Deferring every template-dependent class value whatever its
field names: an unexpected field was then reported only on instantiation, and
not at all in an uncalled template (t13, t13b). (13) Allocating every pending
root before its initializer in this slice: not taken; for the `for` cursor it
reorders the loop header's checking, which no prototype measured (W-264).

FOCUSED RE-REVIEW OF THE FOLD, ROUND 10 (amended 2026-10-20). Owed by no review:
round 9 was dry, and the PR opened as PR 61 and was held. On 2026-10-20 the
fixer of SV-1's plan found X-1 while probing a composition: `match (s)` with a
`case .None` arm on `let s: Opt(T) = Opt(T).None;`, for `choice Opt(T: type) {
Some(value: T), None }`, in `fn Conv[template T: type]` called with an `i32`,
stops the compiler of e408ad4d6 (0.0.0-0.dev+813804758) at the CHECK at
check/pattern_match.cpp:1409, ``Alternative constant type differs from scrutinee
type`` (exit 134), where trunk 0bdce60a5 reports ``semantics TODO: `match on
unsupported scrutinee type` `` (exit 1): an OUT form of the plan's TR-13 turned
into a crash, against R17, so a BLOCKER. A separate fixer reproduced it on the
installed toolchain, on trunk and on the nightly, and hunted the class before
any change: 117 probes over `match`, the `if` and `while` pattern conditions and
`let` ... `else` and every template-dependent scrutinee kind, each run on
e408ad4d6's toolchain, on the fix's, on trunk and on the nightly beside twins
without a template or with a checked parameter, each RUN value derived by hand
first. Root cause: since C4 (D-TP-11) `Opt(T)` is a class type formed in the
definition, which the scrutinee gate admits as it admits a checked generic's,
where trunk's splice of a deferred call is rejected with its TODO; an
alternative pattern's name, for a payload-free alternative or an unknown name,
was then resolved through `PerformMemberAccess`, which adds a deferred
`access_member_action` and a splice for a template-dependent base, so the
engine's check that the arm names an alternative constant of the scrutinee's
type failed; trunk stops the same way for a choice declared in a class template.
Decision, auto-adopted under V-2/V-3 and open to veto: the correct
implementation, not trunk's rejection, because trunk itself runs a class
template's choice in the other refutable forms, so a gate on template dependence
would reject programs trunk runs and turn lanes that e408ad4d6 already ran into
TODOs, while a guard at the CHECK would turn an IN form into a TODO (R17). The
fix commit eafca5cb9 adds `PerformAlternativeAccess`
(refutable_binding.cpp:291-304), which performs the access in the definition
with `PerformAction`, and calls it from the `match` lane and the
pattern-condition lane; it is sound because a choice declares its alternatives
once for every specific. The plan's TR-13 and D-TP-11 are amended: a refutable
pattern on a template-dependent choice or `Core.Int(N)` value is IN, checked in
the definition as a checked generic's is, its payload operations performed on
instantiation; a scrutinee whose type is not known in the definition stays OUT
with trunk's TODO, and W-252 is narrowed to it. _Break:_ a probe of the class
that stops the compiler or runs with a value its twin does not print. Pinned by
check generic/template/match_choice.carbon (23 splits) and lower
template/match_choice.carbon (4 splits), which 74e16c4de fills, and by the tenth
program, templates_match_dependent_choice (twelve EXPECT lines derived by hand);
the mutants that revert either lane or both are killed. One residue is filed
from W-295..W-299, which the orchestrator reserved to TP-1 for the round: W-295,
a checked generic's `Core.Int(N)` compared with an integer literal stops the
compiler while lowering, on trunk and the nightly too; W-296 to W-299 stay
unused. Measured at eafca5cb9 and 74e16c4de, container-built, EXPECTED and not
of record: file_test 1957 passed, 0 failed, "Ran 1957 tests in 79080 ms wall
time", 0 `!` and 0 `?` marks; conformance "PASS 138, COMPILE-FAIL 0, LINK-FAIL
0, RUN-FAIL 0, OUTPUT-MISMATCH 0, DIFF-MISMATCH 0, SKIP 22 (of 160)", bullets

THE DECISIONS, D-DD-1 to D-DD-13, verbatim from fork/designdocs/plan.md §0.5 as
folded through the two plan reviews (A-1 to A-15, B-1, B-2, B-M-1 to B-M-8,
B-m-1 to B-m-8), the two focused re-reviews (RR-A-1, RR-N-1 to RR-N-4, RR-FX-1;
RR2-1 to RR2-3, RR2-FX-1), the document-review fold (DR1-n, DR2-n) and the
second document-review fold (D-DD-2 by DR2b-6, D-DD-7 by R2-3) and the third
(D-DD-2 by DR3b-2, D-DD-9 and D-DD-10 by R3-1 and R3-5); each
break condition is the decision's own, and the `§`, row and finding references
are the plan's:

-   **D-DD-1 Editing posture.** On upstream pages every original paragraph and
    example stays. Only placeholder markers are replaced: the boilerplate
    paragraph and its `## TODO` heading become `## Status` with one dated
    status blockquote; a `TODO:` heading loses its prefix and gains content; a
    TODO-only body that has something to document becomes content (with a
    dated status note before it where no accepted proposal states the rules,
    as in assignment.md); a TODO note beside content becomes a dated note
    only where that note supplies what the marker asks for (README.md :2890,
    settled by F-010; :3911, an inline summary and the updated reference). New
    behavior goes in
    new sections titled "_topic_ in the 0.1 toolchain" (or under the formerly
    empty heading), after the original content. Where an original example is
    rejected by the toolchain, a dated "Fork note" directly after it quotes the
    measured diagnostic and points to the working form. A marker is never
    relabelled or replaced to get past the W2 rule: where a section has nothing
    to document beyond a future extension or a milestone deferral
    (comparison_operators.md "Custom result types"; README.md "Co-routines"
    and "Concurrency", deferred by milestones.md:268 and :271), the upstream
    marker stays and a dated note beside it states the 0.1 status (amended
    2026-10-13, review fold: A-8 / B-M-4; RR-N-3: rev 2's §2.9 item 4
    replaced the Co-routines and Concurrency markers, which this rule now
    forbids, and item 4 keeps them). Break: a
    reviewer shows that a note changes the meaning of accepted proposal text;
    that note is withdrawn and the divergence becomes a residue (D-DD-3).
-   **D-DD-2 Scope and the W2 arbiter.** The arbiter is a script rule over all
    of docs/design/ (§2.12): (a) no line matches the placeholder boilerplate
    (`skeletal design`, `it is a placeholder`, `should not be treated as
    accepted`, `Please feel welcome to rewrite`, and `provisional or
    placeholder`, whitespace-tolerant); (b) no heading's text starts with
    `TODO`; (c) no section's body consists only of TODO-marker paragraphs
    (optionally with "See ..." or "References" paragraphs); and (d) no section
    is empty without a subsection. Every clause matches regardless of case,
    clause (a) also across blockquote line breaks, and clause (c)'s markers
    include TBD and the list-item and HTML-comment forms (clause (d) and these
    extensions amended 2026-10-14, document-review fold: DR2-2 / DR2-8, under
    this decision's break condition: document review 2 showed placeholder
    forms the rule missed; clause (a) also matches after emphasis and code
    markers are removed, clause (b) also takes `TBD` and a heading's leading
    emphasis or code markers, and clause (c)'s companions include a list of
    links after a "See" or "References" paragraph, amended 2026-10-14,
    document-review fold 2: DR2b-6, under the same break condition: document
    review 2 of the second round showed forms the rule still missed; clause
    (c)'s markers also take code markers, and clauses (c) and (d) read a
    section without its HTML comments, multi-line ones included, so that a
    section holding only a comment is empty and a comment whose text is a TODO
    or TBD marker is a marker paragraph, amended 2026-10-14, document-review
    fold 3: DR3b-2, under the same break condition: document review 2 of the
    third round showed forms the rule still missed). Inline notes beside
    content (category C of §0.1c, §0.1f) are out of scope. Two lists qualify
    the result. `QUALIFIED` holds hits that stay by design because a DD-1 note
    in the same section answers them, and the checker requires that note's
    quoted text there: one entry, README.md "This document is provisional"
    (the upstream disclosure, kept under D-DD-1). `ALLOWLIST` holds hits that a
    later commit or a held PR removes, and it shrinks commit by commit (§2.12
    item 5): at commit 3 it holds exactly the two held-PR-owned hits of
    §0.1c (PR 53's Lifetime section, PR 55's arithmetic Strings section), and
    at state L it is empty. An allowlisted hit that no longer hits is itself an
    error (amended 2026-10-13, review fold: A-5 / B-2 / B-M-2 / B-M-3).
    **Deviation from W-065's arbiter, recorded:** W-065's notes call its
    arbiter "grep-verifiable ('no TODO/placeholder markers')"; this rule is
    narrower. Inline TODO, TBD and provisional notes beside content stay
    (category C: 110 `TODO` occurrences in 23 files at 162c7e839, less the
    ones DD-1 replaces), and DD-1's pages add quoted toolchain diagnostics
    that contain `semantics TODO`. The discharge records the before and after
    `TODO` counts per file in the decision-log entry, and row 91's text says
    that the remaining inline notes stay by design (amended 2026-10-13,
    review fold: B-M-4). Break: a document review finds a section a reader
    cannot understand that the rule misses, or a replaced marker that is a
    placeholder under another name; it joins the scope in the fold and the
    rule gains a clause.
-   **D-DD-3 Documentation, not design; F-016 not minted.** Each page states
    what an accepted proposal, a leads decision, or a fork decision fixes,
    what the toolchain does, and where they differ (both cited). A leads
    decision is the answer the leads record on a closed question-for-leads
    issue, which docs/project/evolution.md:425-428 makes "where the leads
    signal how it is resolved"; the page cites the issue and says when no
    proposal incorporates the answer yet. Toolchain defects, including a
    divergence from a leads decision, are residues; open questions stay open
    on the page, and a question is called open only after its issue's status
    has been checked. A behavior that none of these sources rules on is
    stated as measured, never as a rule. Rev 1's assignment text asserted an
    operation order for leads issue 686 without citing the leads' answer; rev
    2 reduced it to the measurements and called the question open; rev 3
    states the answer the leads gave on 2022-11-12 (issue 686's closing
    comment; issue 2489 tracks the proposal that is to incorporate it), which
    gives `(2, 1)` for both literal swaps, and the toolchain's `(2, 2)` as
    W-188 (§2.3, §8.10; amended 2026-10-13, review fold: A-1; RR-A-1). Break:
    if a page cannot be written without choosing a rule that neither a
    proposal, a leads decision, a fork decision, nor the toolchain fixes, the
    page names the open question and a residue is filed; minting F-016 needs
    the orchestrator.
-   **D-DD-4 Sample policy.** Every new code block is a complete Carbon file
    compile-verified on the fork toolchain and on the nightly. A RUNS sample is
